mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) during late-cycle supply constraints signals reduced economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO declines and the economy is in a late cycle (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.0%).

mechanism_narrative: Higher inflation (CPIAUCSL) leads to increased real interest rates and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL (year-over-year) exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.0% in one month signals housing market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST declines > 1.0% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth declines (e.g., -0.5% in last month) and UNRATE rises (e.g., >0.2pp in last month).

mechanism_narrative: Strong economic expansion (GDPC1 growth above 3.0%) in the early cycle drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 quarterly growth (year-over-year) exceeds 3.0%.
